findings: `Dataset.get_tissue` reads the global `mdata.obs`, which the harness' v2 `tabular_inputs` leaves without a `tissue` column (only `response:tissue` after the MuData merge); real and synthetic datasets copy the response obs there (`mdata.obs = response.obs.copy()`). The case does the same itself.

1.6.1 builds the group labels in `DrugResponseDataset._transformation_kwargs` from the `drug_ids` and `tissue` attributes of the dataset being transformed; v2 builds them in `group_labels` from the drug ids of the response batch and `Dataset.get_tissue(sample_ids)` of the dataset being fitted or predicted. For the same pairs the labels are identical, so the transformer is numerically equal (class exact).

1.6.1 fits and applies the transformation after dropping pairs that lack features (`reduce_to`); v2 fits it on the observed pairs of the scope before the featurizers reject pairs (existing v2 behaviour for every transformer, see `tests/models/test_target_transform.py`). The case has features for every pair, so the two coincide here.

1.6.1 trains a single-drug model per drug on that drug's pairs; v2 fits the transformation once over all drugs and routes the drugs inside the predictor. The per-drug offsets are the same, which `single_drug` checks. An unseen drug has no single-drug model in 1.6.1, so it is excluded from that step.
`drevalpy run` fits `NaiveMeanEffectsPredictor` (the normalization reference) on the untransformed response in both versions; that exemption is in the run loop and is not part of this case.
